gap: No result ChatGPT got lines up the single-box 240 V units by whether the 240 V outlet stays live while the unit recharges from an ordinary 120 V outlet or generator. Anker says the F3800 Plus's 240 V output 'cannot be used while the device is charging via 120V AC'. Jackery lists '240V Ports: No Output' for the Explorer 5000 Plus when it charges and discharges at once. BLUETTI says you can 'charge the Apex 300 at 120V without interrupting 240V output'.
standout_why: Watt & Warden (cited) already says split-phase ratings are 'the inverter's combined ceiling, not a per-leg figure'. It also gives F3800 120 V outlets 2,400 W max and the Apex 300 'roughly two 1,920W legs', so per-leg limits are not new. It says nothing about 240 V while charging. Power Station Pilot (cited) gives no per-outlet, surge or charging conditions. StorageReview (cited) has the Apex 300's 14-50R and its 16 ms transfer time, but nothing on 240 V during 120 V charging and no comparison with other units. The Jackery FAQ (cited in the second chat) does state its own '240V Ports: No Output' line. But no page compares across brands, and none of ChatGPT's three answers mentions the condition. It also put the F3800 Plus and the Explorer 5000 Plus as '240V: Yes' with no caveat.
decides: Picture a shopper running a 240 V well pump or other load through a multi-day outage while topping up from a 120 V generator or wall outlet. For that shopper the pick moves to the BLUETTI Apex 300, whose maker says 240 V keeps running during 120 V charging. The Anker S5000 may also qualify, but only on The Gadgeteer's word; Anker's own pages say nothing. The F3800 Plus and the Explorer 5000 Plus drop their 240 V output in that situation. The trade-off: the Apex 300's 3,840 W total is only 16 A at 240 V. So a 240 V load over 16 A (a 24 A EV charger, a 20 A dryer element) still needs the F3800 Plus (25 A stated) or the Explorer 5000 Plus (7,200 W, which is 30 A), run on battery only. The footnote finding: '240V: Yes' means 'yes, on battery' for two of the three units ChatGPT recommended.
